title: Estius and the recent Thomists: grace the total cause
source_text: LXVII. Contra vero Estius & Thomistae recentiores docent gratiam Dei ita esse totalem causam boni operis, ut quicquid est in opere boni totum faciat, & totum opus sit gratiae divinae ascribendum, tanquam causae totali, non solum tanquam partiali.
pass_a_gloss: LXVII. But on the contrary Estius and the more recent Thomists teach that the grace of God is so the total cause of the good work, that whatever of good is in the work it makes the whole, and the whole work is to be ascribed to divine grace, as to total cause, not only as to partial.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXVII. Estius and the more recent Thomists, by contrast, hold that God's grace is the total cause of a good work in such a way that it produces all the good there is in the work. The whole work must therefore be credited to divine grace as its total cause, and not merely as a partial one.

lemmas.gloss: But on the contrary Estius and the more recent Thomists

lemmas.latin: ut quicquid est in opere boni totum faciat
lemmas.gloss: that whatever of good is in the work it makes the whole

lemmas.latin: tanquam causae totali, non solum tanquam partiali
lemmas.gloss: as to total cause, not only as to partial

choices.why: Scholastic terms for a cause that produces the whole effect versus one that produces it only together with a co-cause; Molinists made grace and free choice partial causes.
